If `None`, falls back to `std::env::current_exe()`.\n145\t///\n146\t/// # Returns\n147\t///\n148\t/// * `Result<PathBuf>` - The resolved binary path, or an error if resolution fails.\n149\t///\n150\t/// # Errors\n151\t///\n152\t/// * Returns an error if `worker_binary_path` is `None` and `std::env::current_exe()`\n153\t///   fails (which can happen in some restricted environments or when the binary\n154\t///   has been deleted/moved after launch).\n155\t///\n156\t/// # Examples\n157\t///\n158\t/// ```no_run\n159\t/// use needle::util::resolve_worker_binary_path;\n160\t/// use std::path::PathBuf;\n161\t///\n162\t/// // With explicit override\n163\t/// let override_path = Some(PathBuf::from(\"/custom/path/to/needle\"));\n164\t/// let resolved = resolve_worker_binary_path(override_path.as_ref())\n165\t///     .expect(\"failed to resolve binary path\");\n166\t/// assert_eq!(resolved, PathBuf::from(\"/custom/path/to/needle\"));\n167\t///\n168\t/// // Without override (uses current_exe)\n169\t/// let resolved = resolve_worker_binary_path(None)\n170\t///     .expect(\"failed to resolve current executable\");\n171\t/// ```\n172\tpub fn resolve_worker_binary_path(worker_binary_path: Option<&PathBuf>) -> Result<PathBuf> {\n173\t    if let Some(path) = worker_binary_path {\n174\t        Ok(path.clone())\n175\t    } else {\n176\t        std::env::current_exe()\n177\t            .context(\"failed to resolve worker binary path: current_exe() failed\")\n178\t    }\n179\t}\n180\t\n181\t/// Build a cargo test command with configurable timeout.\n182\t///\n183\t/// This function constructs a `std::process::Command` that runs `cargo test`\n184\t/// with a timeout wrapper. The timeout command will terminate the test if it\n185\t/// exceeds the specified duration.\n186\t///\n187\t/// The command is structured as: `timeout <seconds> cargo test --all-targets -- --nocapture`\n188\t///\n189\t/// # Arguments\n190\t///\n191\t/// * `timeout_minutes` - Optional timeout in minutes. If `None`, defaults to 30 minutes.\n192\t///\n193\t/// # Returns\n194\t///\n195\t/// * `std::process::Command` - Configured command ready for execution via `spawn()` or `status()`.\n196\t///\n197\t/// # Examples\n198\t///\n199\t/// ```no_run\n200\t/// use needle::util::build_cargo_test_command;\n201\t/// use std::process::Command;\n202\t///\n203\t/// // With default 30-minute timeout\n204\t/// let cmd = build_cargo_test_command(None);\n205\t///\n206\t/// // With custom 45-minute timeout\n207\t/// let cmd = build_cargo_test_command(Some(45));\n208\t///\n209\t/// // Execute the command\n210\t/// let status = cmd.status().expect(\"failed to execute cargo test\");\n211\t/// ```\n212\t///\n213\t/// # Timeout Behavior\n214\t///\n215\t/// - The `timeout` command will send `SIGTERM` to the cargo process when the timeout is reached.\n216\t/// - If the process does not exit within 1 second after `SIGTERM`, `SIGKILL` is sent.\n217\t/// - Exit code 124 indicates the timeout was triggered (see `timeout(1)` man page).\n218\t///\n219\t/// # Default Value\n220\t///\n221\t/// When `timeout_minutes` is `None`, the default is **30 minutes**.\n222\tpub fn build_cargo_test_command(timeout_minutes: Option<u64>) -> std::process::Command {\n223\t    let timeout_seconds = timeout_minutes.unwrap_or(30) * 60;\n224\t\n225\t    let mut cmd = std::process::Command::new(\"timeout\");\n226\t    cmd.arg(format!(\"{}\", timeout_seconds))\n227\t        .arg(\"cargo\")\n228\t        .arg(\"test\")\n229\t        .arg(\"--all-targets\")\n230\t        .arg(\"--\")\n231\t        .arg(\"--nocapture\");\n232\t\n233\t    cmd\n234\t}\n235\t\n236\t/// Capture the current system time in UTC as an ISO 8601 formatted string.\n237\t///\n238\t/// Returns the current UTC timestamp as an ISO 8601/RFC 3339 string.\n239\t/// The format is `2026-08-13T14:30:00Z` (UTC timezone indicated by `Z`).\n240\t///\n241\t/// This function handles all errors internally and never panics. If system\n242\t/// time is unavailable or chrono formatting fails (e.g., due to extreme\n243\t/// system clock values that overflow chrono's internal calculations), it\n244\t/// falls back to the Unix epoch timestamp (`1970-01-01T00:00:00Z`) and\n245\t/// logs an error message to stderr.\n246\t///\n247\t/// # Returns\n248\t///\n249\t/// * `String` - Current UTC timestamp in ISO 8601 format, or the epoch\n250\t///   timestamp as a fallback if time capture fails\n251\t///\n252\t/// # Fallback Behavior\n253\t///\n254\t/// When the system time cannot be retrieved (e.g., in restricted environments)\n255\t/// or chrono formatting fails, this function:\n256\t/// - Returns `\"1970-01-01T00:00:00Z\"` (Unix epoch)\n257\t/// - Logs an error message to stderr with failure details\n258\t/// - Never panics, ensuring the function is safe to call in production\n259\t///\n260\t/// # Examples\n261\t///\n262\t/// ```no_run\n263\t/// use needle::util::capture_timestamp;\n264\t///\n265\t/// let now = capture_timestamp();\n266\t/// println!(\"Current UTC time: {}\", now);\n267\t/// // Output: \"2026-08-13T14:30:00Z\" (or epoch on failure)\n268\t/// ```\n269\t///\n270\t/// # Performance\n271\t///\n272\t/// This function performs a system call to get the current time and should\n273\t/// be called only when a timestamp is actually needed.\n274\t///\n275\t/// # Error Handling\n276\t///\n277\t/// For use cases that need to distinguish between success and failure,\n278\t/// use [`capture_timestamp_result()`] instead, which returns a `Result`.\n279\tpub fn capture_timestamp() -> String {\n280\t    capture_timestamp_result().unwrap_or_else(|e| {\n281\t        eprintln!(\"Failed to capture timestamp: {}. Using epoch fallback.\", e);\n282\t        // Unix epoch as ISO 8601 timestamp (fallback when system time fails)\n283\t        \"1970-01-01T00:00:00Z\".to_string()\n284\t    })\n285\t}\n286\t\n287\t/// Capture the current system time in UTC as an ISO 8601 formatted string.\n288\t///\n289\t/// Returns the current UTC timestamp as an ISO 8601/RFC 3339 string.\n290\t/// The format is `2026-08-13T14:30:00Z` (UTC timezone indicated by `Z`).\n291\t///\n292\t/// This is the fallible version of [`capture_timestamp()`] that returns\n293\t/// a `Result` instead of handling errors internally. Use this when you\n294\t/// need to distinguish between successful timestamp capture and failures.\n295\t///\n296\t/// # Returns\n297\t///\n298\t/// * `Result<String>` - Current UTC timestamp in ISO 8601 format, or an\n299\t///   error if time capture fails\n300\t///\n301\t/// # Errors\n302\t///\n303\t/// This function returns an error if:\n304\t/// - The system time cannot be retrieved (e.g., in restricted environments)\n305\t/// - Chrono formatting fails to produce an ISO 8601 string (e.g., due to\n306\t///   extreme system clock values)\n307\t///\n308\t/// # Examples\n309\t///\n310\t/// ```no_run\n311\t/// use needle::util::capture_timestamp_result;\n312\t///\n313\t/// match capture_timestamp_result() {\n314\t///     Ok(timestamp) => println!(\"Current UTC time: {}\", timestamp),\n315\t///     Err(e) => eprintln!(\"Failed to capture timestamp: {}\", e),\n316\t/// }\n317\t/// ```\n318\t///\n319\t/// # Performance\n320\t///\n321\t/// This function performs a system call to get the current time and should\n322\t/// be called only when a timestamp is actually needed.\n323\tpub fn capture_timestamp_result() -> Result<String> {\n324\t    // Use catch_unwind to handle any potential panics from chrono operations\n325\t    // This protects against extreme edge cases like system clock overflow\n326\t    let result = std::panic::catch_unwind(std::panic::AssertUnwindSafe(|| {\n327\t        let now = chrono::Utc::now();\n328\t        now.to_rfc3339_opts(chrono::SecondsFormat::Secs, true)\n329\t    }));\n330\t\n331\t    match result {\n332\t        Ok(timestamp) => Ok(timestamp),\n333\t        Err(_) => Err(anyhow::anyhow!(\n334\t            \"chrono operation panicked - possibly due to extreme system clock values\"\n335\t        )),\n336\t    }\n337\t}\n338\t\n339\t/// Crate-wide test-only environment isolation.\n340\t///\n341\t/// `HOME` is process-global, but Rust runs unit tests as threads inside a\n342\t/// single process. Any test that calls `set_var(\"HOME\", ..)` or\n343\t/// `remove_var(\"HOME\")` therefore mutates state that every concurrently\n344\t/// running test observes. Before this module existed, several modules each\n345\t/// had their own private `Mutex` (or none at all), which provides no mutual\n346\t/// exclusion against the others — tests that merely *read* `HOME`\n347\t/// (`worker::tests`, `telemetry::tests`, tilde expansion) failed\n348\t/// nondeterministically depending on interleaving.\n349\t///\n350\t/// Every test that reads or writes `HOME`/`PATH` must go through\n351\t/// [`isolate_env`] or [`isolate_env_with_home`] so that exactly one such test\n352\t/// runs at a time and the previous values are always restored.\n353\t#[cfg(test)]\n354\tpub(crate) mod test_env {\n355\t    use std::ffi::OsString;\n356\t    use std::sync::{Mutex, MutexGuard};\n357\t\n358\t    /// The single process-wide lock guarding `HOME`/`PATH` in tests.\n359\t    static ENV_LOCK: Mutex<()> = Mutex::new(());\n360\t\n361\t    /// Restores `HOME` and `PATH` to their captured values when dropped.\n362\t    pub(crate) struct EnvGuard {\n363\t        home: Option<OsString>,\n364\t        path: Option<OsString>,\n365\t    }\n366\t\n367\t    impl Drop for EnvGuard {\n368\t        fn drop(&mut self) {\n369\t            restore(\"HOME\", self.home.take());\n370\t            restore(\"PATH\", self.path.take());\n371\t        }\n372\t    }\n373\t\n374\t    fn restore(key: &str, value: Option<OsString>) {\n375\t        match value {\n376\t            Some(value) => std::env::set_var(key, value),\n377\t            None => std::env::remove_var(key),\n378\t        }\n379\t    }\n380\t\n381\t    /// A private, per-caller NEEDLE home for tests.\n382\t    ///\n383\t    /// `WorkspaceConfig::default_home()` resolves to the operator's real\n384\t    /// `~/.needle`, whose `state/workers.json` is the *live fleet's* worker\n385\t    /// registry. Unit tests that construct a `Worker` therefore registered\n386\t    /// themselves into it and raced each other (and the running fleet) on a\n387\t    /// single read-modify-write file. Every test config must point somewhere\n388\t    /// private instead.\n389\t    ///\n390\t    /// Each call returns a fresh subdirectory, so concurrently running tests\n391\t    /// that share a worker id never touch the same registry file. The backing\n392\t    /// root is held in a `OnceLock` for the lifetime of the test process.\n393\t    pub(crate) fn isolated_home() -> std::path::PathBuf {\n394\t        use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicUsize, Ordering};\n395\t        use std::sync::OnceLock;\n396\t\n397\t        static ROOT: OnceLock<tempfile::TempDir> = OnceLock::new();\n398\t        static NEXT: AtomicUsize = AtomicUsize::new(0);\n399\t\n400\t        let root =\n401\t            ROOT.get_or_init(|| tempfile::tempdir().expect(\"failed to create test home root\"));\n402\t        let dir = root\n403\t            .path()\n404\t            .join(format!(\"home-{}\", NEXT.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed)));\n405\t        std::fs::create_dir_all(dir.join(\"state\")).expect(\"failed to create test home state dir\");\n406\t        dir\n407\t    }\n408\t\n409\t    /// Acquire the environment lock and capture `HOME`/`PATH` for restoration.\n410\t    ///\n411\t    /// Hold the returned tuple for the whole test body; dropping it releases\n412\t    /// the lock and restores the environment. The lock is intentionally\n413\t    /// poison-tolerant: a panicking test must not wedge every later test.\n414\t    pub(crate) fn isolate_env() -> (MutexGuard<'static, ()>, EnvGuard) {\n415\t        let lock = ENV_LOCK\n416\t            .lock()\n417\t            .unwrap_or_else(|poisoned| poisoned.into_inner());\n418\t        let guard = EnvGuard {\n419\t            home: std::env::var_os(\"HOME\"),\n420\t            path: std::env::var_os(\"PATH\"),\n421\t        };\n422\t        (lock, guard)\n423\t    }\n424\t}\n425\t\n426\t#[cfg(test)]\n427\tmod tests {\n428\t Unit tests that construct a `Worker` therefore registered\n    /// themselves into it and raced each other (and the running fleet) on a\n    /// single read-modify-write file. Every test config must point somewhere\n    /// private instead.\n    ///\n    /// Each call returns a fresh subdirectory, so concurrently running tests\n    /// that share a worker id never touch the same registry file. The backing\n    /// root is held in a `OnceLock` for the lifetime of the test process.\n    pub(crate) fn isolated_home() -> std::path::PathBuf {\n        use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicUsize, Ordering};\n        use std::sync::OnceLock;\n\n        static ROOT: OnceLock<tempfile::TempDir> = OnceLock::new();\n        static NEXT: AtomicUsize = AtomicUsize::new(0);\n\n        let root =\n            ROOT.get_or_init(|| tempfile::tempdir().expect(\"failed to create test home root\"));\n        let dir = root\n            .path()\n            .join(format!(\"home-{}\", NEXT.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed)));\n        std::fs::create_dir_all(dir.join(\"state\")).expect(\"failed to create test home state dir\");\n        dir\n    }\n\n    /// Acquire the environment lock and capture `HOME`/`PATH` for restoration.\n    ///\n    /// Hold the returned tuple for the whole test body; dropping it releases\n    /// the lock and restores the environment. The lock is intentionally\n    /// poison-tolerant: a panicking test must not wedge every later test.\n    pub(crate) fn isolate_env() -> (MutexGuard<'static, ()>, EnvGuard) {\n        let lock = ENV_LOCK\n            .lock()\n            .unwrap_or_else(|poisoned| poisoned.into_inner());\n        let guard = EnvGuard {\n            home: std::env::var_os(\"HOME\"),\n            path: std::env::var_os(\"PATH\"),\n        };\n        (lock, guard)\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n    use chrono::{Datelike, Timelike};\n    use std::env;\n    use
